findings.title: With no stored state, an interrupted adoption becomes "already planned" and can't be resumed
findings.description:
Detection is "derived from the files every time". Any architecture doc or slice plan makes a project "already planned" (line 76). The adoption flow writes the concept, then the architecture, then the slice plan (line 91), in that order. If the session dies or the PM stops after the derived architecture is written but before the existing-state slice plan, the project already reads as "already planned":

- `sq onboard` step 2 (line 88) then says adoption doesn't apply.
- `cf next` navigates it as a normal planned project. It recommends ordinary slice planning, and nothing tells the agent to record built work as retroactive.

The amendment removed the one thing that covered this. The original guide contract (line 136) said "a re-run resumes from whatever artifacts exist", and the `in_progress` state held that position. The amendment keeps no replacement. "An adopted project lands here, so no completion state is needed" (line 76) only holds when the run finishes.

The arch has to pick a rule, because squadron will build `sq onboard` against it (slice 271). Options:
- Make "already planned" need a slice plan, or a non-derived architecture (`provenance: derived` already exists, slice 263 D7).
- Report a fourth outcome, "partially adopted": a derived architecture with no slice plan that has retroactive entries.
- Require the flow to write the slice plan before, or atomically with, the architecture.

findings.title: Sections said to be "rewritten to match" still describe the old `cf build` design
findings.description:
The amendment (line 24) says "the sections below are rewritten to match". Several still state the superseded design as if it were current:

- **Guide release coupling (line 137):** "If cf selects the brownfield profile … `cf build` fails with a named error." This contradicts "cf build is pure again" (line 27). The parenthetical says the rule "moves to the prompt-delivery primitive", but the normative sentence was never rewritten, so the actual rule is unstated.
- **Dependencies (line 159):** "cf releases that select the brownfield profile require at least v0.22.2". After 268, no cf release selects that profile. v0.22.1/v0.22.2 are justified by the probe's `surfaces.<s>.concept` and the "squadron-path gate", both of which this rework deletes. The real guide minimum for the rework (slice 272 raises `MIN_GUIDE_VERSION`) isn't stated.
- **Squadron contract stability (line 135) and Guide prompt contract (line 136):** most of their text is "for history": the full probe schema, `commits_behind` policy and the Adoption Facts layout. The arch is the thing slice designs follow. Keeping retired contracts inline, in normative voice, makes a slice designer likely to build against the wrong one. Move them to the DEVLOG or the slice plan's Notes.
- **Anticipated Slices (lines 145-153):** still lists "persisted adoption state", "`cf build` selecting the `brownfield-adoption` profile", "reading the probe" and "adoption steps while in progress" as the plan. The rework slices 268–272 get only a one-line preface.

findings.title: "Current State" describes the codebase before 260–267, not the code the rework removes
findings.description:
Current State still says the three onboarding copies "already drift" and that `cf next` treats sparse planning state as a fresh project. Slices 260–267 are shipped (slice plan, all `[x]`). The current state that matters for the rework isn't described anywhere in the arch:

- `adoption.state` with four values in `ConfigKeys.ts`
- `adoptionResolver.ts`, `adoptionCompletion.ts`, `adoptionFacts.ts`
- `adoptionNavigation.ts` (about 240 lines)
- the probe code
- the build-time state writes

So the arch can't be checked for whether the rework removes all of it. For example, `planningArtifacts.ts:35` still tells users "To skip detection run `cf config set adoption.state in_progress`", which becomes a wrong remedy after 269. The arch says nothing about it.

findings.title: Migrating shipped `adoption.state` values isn't covered, and the slice plan contradicts itself
findings.description:
The arch says "The only stored value is the opt-out" but never says where it lives, or what happens to configs that already hold `in_progress`, `complete` or `declined` from the shipped 0.19.x releases.

Slice 269 has existing values "ignored with a one-time notice". "One-time" needs a stored "notice shown" flag, which breaks the arch's "nothing persists" rule. Meanwhile the slice plan's Notes still say "No migration of user data: the adoption state … [is a] new format".

This is a change to a config-key format that users depend on. The arch should decide:
- the key and type of the opt-out
- whether `declined` maps to it
- that stale values produce a warning on every read until removed (stateless), not a one-time notice

findings.title: cf finds the comprehension doc by squadron's filename and `docType`, though squadron could pass the path
findings.description:
The principle says cf never parses squadron output or inspects squadron's paths. Then it makes squadron's file-naming convention (`{n}-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md`), its `docType` and "squadron 361's provenance block" (line 119) a cf-side contract. In the flow, squadron writes that doc in step 3 and calls cf in step 4 (lines 89-90), so squadron already knows the path.

Have the prompt-delivery primitive take the comprehension path as a parameter. That removes cf's discovery code and the cross-repo filename coupling, and leaves "found by filename and docType" only as a possible later fallback. As designed, cf breaks silently if squadron renames the file. The doc then "doesn't resolve" and the prompt runs "from the repo alone" (line 136) with no error.

findings.title: The new cross-repo contract has no version field and no defined failure modes
findings.description:
The old probe contract had `probe_version`, null semantics, exit-code meaning and a rule that "unknown version → stated, never silent" (line 135). Its replacement, cf's project-state report and prompt delivery (line 135: "the contract … is now cf's detection report and prompt delivery"), has none of these. The arch doesn't specify:

- **A schema version in the JSON**, which squadron needs to detect an older or newer cf.
- **The error shape when detection fails.** `findPlanningArtifacts` throws `AdoptionError` on an unreadable directory. Does the CLI exit non-zero, and what does the MCP tool return?
- **What happens with an unregistered project.** `sq onboard` step 2 may run before `cf init` succeeds.
- **The error when the guide lacks the adoption prompt.** Line 53 requires an error but doesn't say what squadron receives.

Slice 271 is flagged "the contract squadron will build against". The arch should fix these properties rather than leave them all to slice design.

findings.title: The prompt-delivery primitive is under-specified and risks a second template engine
findings.description:
The guide's `brownfield-adoption` asset is a context profile with four file variables (`fileConcept`, `fileArch`, `fileSlicePlan`, `fileComprehension`), and its resume logic depends on them. The arch says the new primitive delivers "the adoption prompt by key, with the comprehension doc's path filled in". That fills one variable, and it defers "how the profile's variables are delivered" to slice 271.

That choice decides whether the guide prompt must be rewritten (coordinated in 272) and whether resume still works (see the FAIL). It also risks a second variable-substitution path beside `ContextTemplateEngine`.

The arch should pick one:
- an explicit, read-only profile render through the existing engine (for example, building a named profile with no phase or state side effects), or
- plain prompt text plus a documented variable set.

It should not leave the choice to a slice. The choice also affects whether "cf build keeps one meaning" (line 42) means "no implicit profile swap" or "no profile rendering at all".

findings.title: The ownership table gives cf "ownership" of artifacts cf never writes
findings.description:
- **Row (c):** "CF writes the architecture doc on both paths … One writer." There is now one path (line 31), and cf writes nothing. The agent writes the doc from a guide prompt that squadron fetched.
- **Row (d):** cf owns the existing-state slice plan, which the agent also writes.
- **The retroactive marker** is "set only by the adoption flow" (line 100). cf can't enforce that. Only slice 263 D4's structural checks limit it.
- **The Concept row:** "nothing overwrites an existing concept without the PM saying so." No component is named to enforce this now that cf isn't in the loop.

Restate the table in terms of what each party provides: cf the format spec, parser, checker and prompt delivery; the guide the prompt text; squadron the orchestration and the PM gate. For each "never" rule, name which component enforces it, or say it is enforced by the prompt only.

findings.title: Slice 274 is called the benefit that justifies adoption, but the arch has no goal or design for it
findings.description:
The slice plan says carrying comprehension into later phases "is the benefit that justifies adoption at all" (274). The arch's Design Goals and Envisioned State never mention it. Its stated core goal is "`cf next` pointing at new work" (line 145). The arch is also silent on how the comprehension doc stays fresh or how later profiles reach it. Slice 274 calls this a "three-repo contract", but no architecture covers it.

Either add it to the goals and give it a sketch (variables, a staleness signal, owner), or drop the "justifies adoption" claim from the slice plan.

findings.title: Detection on every `cf next`, and the opt-out in worktrees
findings.description:
- `cf next` now runs detection on every call so it can print the brownfield line. The source-volume floor (line 73) keeps this cheap, so it's fine as designed.
- The opt-out is the only stored value, and project config is stored per checkout directory. Opting out in one git worktree won't carry to another, so each worktree keeps showing the line. Say whether that's intended.
- The line points at `sq onboard`, which doesn't exist yet. The wording should make clear the command isn't available yet, so agents don't try to run it.

findings.title: Shipped reconciliation (266) and docs mapping (267) lose their entry point
findings.description: Slice 266 adds a persisted resolution format that `setup-ide` applies, and slice 267 adds `050-docs-map`. Both shipped, and both were meant to be reached through adoption. With adoption parked and `cf next` carrying no adoption guidance, nothing leads a user to them (266's own Future Work lists the missing `cf next` hint). That's acceptable, but the arch should say they stay live and stand alone.
